Subject: Invoice delivery preference for PO-987654 (City of Westport)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the call earlier. City of Westport needs to confirm how Redwood will submit invoices for the contract tied to PO-987654. Our AP team requires the following options to be clear:

- Preferred: E-invoice submission via our SFTP/portal (audit trail required).
- Acceptable: Signed PDF invoice emailed to accounts-payable@westport.gov, with LOA from Redwood confirming authorization to bill against PO-987654.

A few constraints: invoices must include a clear tax breakdown (line-level VAT) and reference the PO number on the invoice body and filename. For some projects we require a reverse-charge annotation; can Redwood include that when needed?

Attached: PO-987654.pdf (purchase order)

Can you confirm what you can support and what the enrollment timeline looks like? We may need an LOA on city letterhead before enabling portal push.

Subject: Re: Invoice delivery preference for PO-987654 (City of Westport)

Hi Helen — appreciated the context and the PO.

Short answer: we can support both options. Recommendations and constraints below so AP has a clear playbook.

1) Portal / SFTP (recommended for government contracts)
- Benefits: signed audit trail, automatic PO matching, less manual touch for your AP team.
- Enrollment: we need a Letter of Authorization (LOA) signed by City procurement to authorize Redwood to push invoices on your behalf. Once we have the LOA plus a test endpoint (SFTP creds or API/PEPPOL ID), we can enable portal auto-push; typical setup 3-7 business days.
- File format: PDF or UBL (we support PEPPOL/UBL, SFTP-delivered PDFs, and e-invoice payloads). We can include line-level tax breakdown and a reverse-charge field if you confirm the tax regime details.

2) Email (fallback)
- We can email a signed PDF to accounts-payable@westport.gov and optionally Bcc your AP inbox with 'invoices@redwood.com' for records. This is fine for single invoices but increases AP friction.

Next steps I propose:
- If City is OK with portal enrollment: please send the LOA and a sample test endpoint (SFTP/PEPPOL id) + the remit bank details you expect on the invoice.
- If City prefers email-only: confirm the signatory name and whether the PO must be visible on the filename and subject (we can enforce both).

Ive looped in Kimberly (billing lead) and Ben (collections) to handle the enrollment and verify tax handling. Ive attached our sample invoice template so you can confirm fields.

Attachments: sample-invoice-template.pdf

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
--

Sofia / Ben — following up with ops details for City of Westport:

Checklist for portal enrollment (what we need from City):
- Signed LOA on letterhead (authorizes invoice submission for PO-987654)
- Test SFTP creds or PEPPOL ID + endpoint contact
- Remit-to bank details and legal name to print on invoice
- VAT/Tax ID and indication whether reverse-charge applies (line-level)

Our recommended config: enable portal auto-push to City SFTP + simultaneous email copy to accounts-payable@westport.gov for the first 2 billing cycles. That gives AP a soft landing and lets us confirm matching rules.

Technical notes:
- File naming convention we will use: WESTPORT_PO-987654_Redwood_YYYYMMDD_invoice.pdf (we can change per procurement rules).
- PDF will include signed name (automated e-sign) and full tax breakdown. If City requires UBL, we can include a UBL XML payload alongside the PDF.

Ben — can you confirm we have the signer authority on file for Redwood (who signs on behalf of Redwood for municipal contracts)? If not, we need to produce a short LOA for City to sign that names our authorized invoice submitter. Ill attach the internal checklist I use for gov enrollments.

Attachments: gov-invoice-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Billing Manager, Redwood Inference

- a summary line that reads: "Reverse charge applies under Article 194 - City of Westport" (we will confirm exact language if needed)
